reviews.text: Salam aleykum wa rahmatoullah ! Aujourd'hui le 28/08/2026 en ce moment où j'écris ce commentaire je suis devant la mosquée et je suis déçue des gens qui gère cette mosquée. Je suis un chauffeur uber et en passant j'ai vu sur google la mosquée la plus proche pour me rendre pour la prière de icha et ça m'a indiqué à la mosquée. Donc je suis venu à 21h34 devant la porte j'ai vu des gens ont déjà fini la prière et sont entrain de discuter juste devant la porte d'entrée à l'intérieur et l'un d'entre eux m'a ouvert la porte, en suite y'avait un homme noir élancé avec des barbe noir et blanche. Et il me demande vous êtes venu pourquoi ? Soubhannallah j'étais choqué de cette question et j'ai juste répondu je suis venu pour prier biensûr, puis il m'a dit non vous ne pouvez pas prier puisqu'il faut respecter l'heure de prière et je lui ai dit je sais pas l'heure à laquelle vous prier, je suis juste de passage car je suis un chauffeur uber. Il a insisté que je retourne et je ne peux pas effectuer la prière. Mais j'ai vu sur google que la mosquée se ferme à 22h15. J'étais énervé puis j'étais sorti sans rien dire découragé, y'avait même un homme qui m'a trouvé dehors et m'a dit c'est pas logique et pourtant ils sont encore là a causé. Franchement dans quel monde on est, refusé à quelqu'un d'effectuer la prière juste de 5min. Il faut vraiment les responsables de la mosquée voient ça. Merci !
reviews.textTranslated: Peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah! Today, August 28, 2026, as I write this comment, I am standing in front of the mosque and I am disappointed with the people who manage it. I am an Uber driver, and while passing by, I looked up the nearest mosque on Google for Isha prayer, and it directed me to this one. So I arrived at 9:34 PM. I saw people who had already finished praying and were chatting right in front of the entrance. Inside, one of them opened the door for me, and then there was a tall, dark-skinned man with a black and white beard. He asked me, "Why have you come?" Subhanallah, I was shocked by that question and I just replied, "I came to pray, of course." Then he told me, "No, you can't pray because you have to respect the prayer times." I told him, "I don't know what time you pray; I'm just passing through because I'm an Uber driver." He insisted I go back and that I couldn't perform the prayer. But I saw on Google that the mosque closes at 10:15 PM. I was angry and left without saying anything, discouraged. There was even a man who found me outside and said, "It doesn't make sense," and yet they're still there talking. Honestly, what kind of world do we live in? Refusing someone the chance to pray for just five minutes? The mosque officials really need to see this. Thank you!

reviews.text:
As-salamu ‘alaykum wa rahmatullah,
Je suis venu prier aujourd’hui à la mosquée à l'heure du Aasr et je voulais simplement partager un petit commentaire constructif. En arrivant, je n’ai vu aucune indication sur les portes précisant quelle entrée ou quelle salle était réservée aux hommes ou aux femmes. Je me suis donc trompé et je suis monté dans la salle du haut pour prier.
Alhamdulillah, il n’y avait aucune femme dans la salle pendant ma prière. C’est seulement après avoir terminé, en voyant des jeunes filles entrer, que j’ai compris que cette salle était probablement réservée aux femmes. Je leur ai demandé et elles m’ont confirmé que les hommes priaient en bas.
Ce serait très apprécié de mettre une affiche ou une indication claire sur les portes afin d’éviter que d’autres personnes fassent la même erreur à l’avenir.
Jazakumullahu khayran pour vos efforts et pour tout ce que vous faites pour la communauté.
reviews.textTranslated:
As-salamu ‘alaykum wa rahmatullah,
I came to pray at the mosque today at the time of Asr and I just wanted to share a small, constructive comment. Upon arriving, I didn't see any signs on the doors indicating which entrance or room was reserved for men or women. So, I made a mistake and went up to the upstairs room to pray.
Alhamdulillah, there were no women in the room during my prayer. It was only after I finished, when I saw some young girls entering, that I realized this room was probably reserved for women. I asked them, and they confirmed that the men pray downstairs.
It would be greatly appreciated if you could put up a sign or a clear indication on the doors to prevent others from making the same mistake in the future. Jazakumullahu khayran for your efforts and for everything you do for the community.

reviews.name: Eman Alsharifi
reviews.text:
This review is not about the mosque itself, as the mosque is a house of Allah and deserves respect. It is about the employee حفيظة (Hafidha) and the mosque administration because of the way my complaint was handled.

I had a very difficult experience with حفيظة (Hafidha), involving words and behavior that included describing me with a very serious and hurtful label. Perhaps for her it was just an incident that ended, or a way she has become accustomed to treating some female worshippers. But her actions had a real impact on us and ultimately led to a family that regularly attended the mosque being deprived of praying there. This is not something insignificant for Allah.

What was even more disappointing was the administration’s response. I was promised that my complaint would be investigated, but I did not receive the attention or follow-up I expected.

I hope حفيظة (Hafidha) reflects on the impact of her actions, and that the mosque administration takes worshippers’ complaints seriously. Those working in a house of Allah have an even greater responsibility to treat people with respect, protect their dignity, and facilitate their worship—not make them feel unwelcome.

Allah knows what happened, and no right is ever lost before Him.
